questions: Did the sensor row ever read all-background (sum below 0.05) on any track? If so, on which section?
Was the signal linear across the tape, or did it saturate or flatten at the edges of the sensor span?
Did the robot hit the wheel torque or turn-rate limit on tight bends? Did it understeer or oscillate?
Is the sensor row too close to the axle, or is the lookahead too short for the speed reached?

intent: Establish a baseline, symmetric, five-sensor front row with overlapping 12 mm footprints and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] that are proportional to lateral position. Hypothesis: this geometry gives a clean, nearly linear signal across the tape, so the Integrator can tune a stable controller without fighting sensor dead zones. Next iteration I will adjust sensor spacing or forward offset based on the observed line-loss events and oscillation, and widen or narrow the wheel track if turn authority proves to be the limit.
learning: Baseline iteration. No prior evidence. Record which sensors dominate the signal and whether the 0.08 m sensing span is wider or narrower than needed.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. The design therefore starts from first principles. Five sensors in a single row 0.04 m ahead of the axle, spaced 0.02 m apart (x = -0.04 to +0.04), give a sensing span of 0.08 m. With 12 mm footprints, adjacent sensors overlap and the 25 mm tape is always covered by at least two or three sensors, which keeps the signal continuous on bends and avoids line-loss on small offsets. Forward placement at y = 0.04 gives some lookahead, so steering starts before the wheels reach a bend. Weights are [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] in left-positive order, so the signal is proportional to lateral offset and its magnitude stays within the allowed range. The wheel track of 0.12 m and wheel radius of 0.03 m are mid-range values that give a moderate turn authority. Body width of 0.12 m widens the off-track limit to max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, so the robot can drift a little further before the run ends. Mass of 0.8 kg and body length of 0.18 m are mid-range. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with modest rms_error, provided the Integrator's gains keep the robot within about 0.03 m of the line. Speed is set by the controller, not by this geometry, so I am not specifying base_speed here.
